summary: South Korean crypto savings, lending, and staking platform that suspended customer withdrawals in June 2023 following stress linked to Haru Invest, received a three-month FIU business suspension and monetary penalty, failed to obtain rehabilitation, and was declared bankrupt by the Seoul Bankruptcy Court in November 2024.
what_happened: Delio operated centralized crypto deposit, yield, lending, and staking products. It halted withdrawals on 14 June 2023 after Haru Invest suspended services and market and counterparty stress spread through the Korean yield sector. Korean regulators later imposed business-suspension and monetary sanctions. The Seoul Rehabilitation Court rejected rehabilitation applications in April 2024 after finding continued operations and going-concern value too uncertain. On 22 November 2024, the court declared Delio bankrupt, moving the case into liquidation and creditor-claim administration.
uncertainty_notes: The February 2018 date reflects the approximate company-establishment period rather than a verified first day of every customer product. Delio discussed phased or limited withdrawal resumptions after the initial halt, but those announcements did not restore normal platform-wide liquidity. Customer ownership treatment, realizable assets, counterparty recoveries, and final distribution rates remain subject to the Korean bankruptcy process.
notes: Added as a major South Korean centralized crypto-yield failure with documented withdrawal suspension, regulatory sanctions, failed rehabilitation, and court-declared bankruptcy.
